question: Can a small code model trained on a small amount of 'textbook quality' data (filtered and GPT-3.5-synthesised) match much larger code models on HumanEval and MBPP?
hypothesis: Language models benefit from training data that is clear, self-contained, instructive and balanced, like a good textbook; data quality can beat scale.
contributions: phi-1, a 1.3B code model reaching 50.6% HumanEval and 55.5% MBPP pass@1 with ~7B unique tokens
Data recipe: LM-classifier-filtered Stack/StackOverflow plus GPT-3.5 synthetic textbooks (CodeTextbook) and synthetic exercises (CodeExercises) for finetuning
Evidence of emergent capability after finetuning on exercises, an LLM-graded unconventional benchmark, and a similarity-pruning decontamination study

method.summary: Decoder-only 1.3B transformer pretrained on CodeTextbook (6B filtered web code tokens + <1B GPT-3.5 textbook tokens) for ~8 epochs, then finetuned on ~180M tokens of GPT-3.5 synthetic Python exercises (CodeExercises). Quality filter is a random forest on CodeGen embeddings trained on ~100k GPT-4 educational-value annotations.
method.task: Python function completion from docstrings (code LM pretraining and finetuning)

datasets.name: The Stack (Python, deduplicated) + StackOverflow
datasets.preprocessing: Filtered with a random-forest quality classifier on pretrained codegen output embeddings, labels from GPT-4 on ~100k samples ('educational value for a student whose goal is to learn basic coding concepts'); filtered subset ~6B tokens

datasets.name: Synthetic textbook (GPT-3.5)
datasets.source: generated by GPT-3.5; diversity via constraints on topic and target audience; some generation details withheld

datasets.name: CodeExercises (GPT-3.5)
datasets.source: generated by GPT-3.5; diversity via constrained function names; each exercise is a function docstring to complete
datasets.preprocessing: Pruned versions for decontamination study (removes 42.5K to 354K of 879.5K problems)

datasets.name: 50 new unconventional problems
datasets.source: written by a dedicated team with no access to CodeExercises or the final model

models.name: phi-1
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer, FlashAttention MHA, parallel MHA and MLP, rotary embeddings (rotary dim 32)

models.name: phi-1-base
models.architecture: as phi-1; checkpoint at 24,000 steps of pretraining on CodeTextbook

other.uses: annotates 100k samples for quality filter; grades Section 4 solutions 0-10

models.name: StarCoder, StarCoder-Prompted, WizardCoder, Replit, CodeGen-Mono, CodeT5+ and others

training.objective: next-token prediction; files concatenated into one array separated by <|endoftext|>, sliced into sequences
training.batch_size: effective 1024 pretraining; 256 finetuning (including data parallelism and gradient accumulation)
training.steps: pretraining 36,000 total, checkpoint at 24,000 used as phi-1-base; finetuning 6,000, best checkpoint chosen (saved every 1000)
training.tokens: little over 50B total pretraining tokens seen (51B in Fig 2.1 caption); finetuning on <200M-token dataset
training.compute: 770 GPU hours for phi-1/phi-1-base (51B tokens); 1090 GPU hours for The Stack+ baseline (76B tokens)
training.wall_clock: phi-1-base under 4 days; finetuning additional 7 hours

other.finetuning_selection: best checkpoint picked, selection data not stated

inference.samples: one generation per problem (pass@1 'using only one LLM generation')
inference.prompting: HumanEval docstring completion; grader prompt asks GPT-4 for a short verbal evaluation then a grade 0-10 (prompt text not printed)

parameters.similarity_threshold_tau: AST match rate 0.95, 0.9, 0.85, 0.8; embedding distance threshold fixed but value not stated

metrics.name: pass@1 HumanEval

metrics.definition: GPT-4 grades solution 0 to 10 after a short verbal evaluation, on 50 unconventional problems

limits: Specialised to Python; weak on specific APIs and less common packages (Conclusion)
Less robust to prompt style, grammatical mistakes and long prompts; poor at counting and spatial reasoning (Appendix B)
GPT-3.5 synthetic data has a high error rate; authors suggest GPT-4 would help
Synthetic data generation details withheld for proprietary reasons, and data not released; not reproducible from the paper
No ablation isolating synthetic textbooks from filtering at 1.3B, no seeds or error bars, decoding settings not stated
Authors concede they lack a good methodology to measure diversity and redundancy of the data
Emergent-capability claims in Section 3 are qualitative examples only
HumanEval score gain is partly attributed to CodeExercises; Table 3 shows lower accuracy on non-similar problems for all models
